title: Grade 3 Science — Wed, May 27
description: States of Matter — Solid, Liquid, Gas — Day 3 of 5
subject: science

questions.question: What are the three states of matter?
questions.explanation: Everything around us exists in one of three states: solid, liquid, or gas.

questions.question: Which state of matter has a fixed shape?
questions.explanation: Solids have a fixed, definite shape. They don't change shape unless force is applied. Example: stone, ice.

questions.question: Water is a liquid. What happens when water is heated?
questions.explanation: When water is heated to 100°C, it turns into water vapour (steam) — changing from liquid to gas.

questions.question: Which of these is a GAS?
questions.explanation: Air is a gas — it has no fixed shape or size and fills any container.

questions.question: What happens to water when it freezes?
questions.explanation: Water freezes at 0°C and becomes ice (solid). Liquid to solid change is called freezing.

questions.question: Liquids:
options: Take the shape of their container
questions.explanation: Liquids take the shape of whatever container they're in, but their volume stays the same.

questions.question: What do we call the change from liquid to solid?
questions.explanation: Freezing is when a liquid changes to a solid by losing heat. Water freezes to form ice.

questions.question: What do we call the change from solid to liquid?
questions.explanation: Melting is when a solid absorbs heat and changes to a liquid. Ice melts to become water.

questions.question: Can gases be compressed (squeezed into a smaller space)?
questions.explanation: Gases can be compressed — the particles are far apart. This is why we can pump air into tyres.

questions.question: Which of these is a SOLID?
questions.explanation: Wood is a solid — it has a fixed shape and size.

questions.question: Ice cream left outside on a hot day will:
questions.explanation: Heat causes ice cream (solid) to melt and become a liquid — this is a change of state (solid → liquid).

questions.question: What is evaporation?
options: Liquid changing to gas (slowly, at the surface)
questions.explanation: Evaporation is when a liquid slowly changes to gas at its surface. Puddles dry up by evaporation.

questions.question: Which property is TRUE of all gases?
options: They fill the entire space of their container
questions.explanation: Gases have no fixed shape or volume — they spread out to fill any container completely.

questions.question: What is condensation?
questions.explanation: Condensation is when gas (water vapour) cools and becomes liquid. Water droplets on a cold glass are condensation.

questions.question: Which state of matter do particles move MOST in?
questions.explanation: Gas particles move the fastest and are furthest apart. Solid particles vibrate in place but don't move freely.
